description: This topic traces how Tanganyikans moved from early welfare associations through TANU and constitutional struggle under Julius Nyerere to win peaceful independence on 9 December 1961 and become a republic in 1962.

mcq.questionText: Which political organisation was formed in 1954 to lead Tanganyika's struggle for independence?
mcq.explanation: TANU was founded on 7 July 1954, growing out of the Tanganyika African Association, to demand self-government and independence.

mcq.questionText: Who was the first president of TANU and the leader of Tanganyika's independence movement?
mcq.explanation: Julius Nyerere became the first president of TANU in 1954 and led the country to independence in 1961.

mcq.questionText: On what date did Tanganyika achieve full independence?
mcq.explanation: Tanganyika became fully independent on 9 December 1961, with Julius Nyerere as Prime Minister.

mcq.questionText: From which earlier organisation did TANU mainly develop?
mcq.explanation: TANU was a transformation of the Tanganyika African Association, turning a welfare body into a mass political party.

mcq.questionText: Under whose administration was Tanganyika governed as a United Nations Trust Territory after the Second World War?
mcq.explanation: After 1946 Tanganyika was a UN Trust Territory administered by Britain, which was obliged to prepare it for self-rule.

mcq.questionText: Which language did TANU use to unite people of different tribes during the independence struggle?
mcq.explanation: Kiswahili was a common language across many tribes, so TANU used it to spread its message and build national unity.

mcq.questionText: Which method did TANU mainly use to demand independence from the British?
mcq.explanation: TANU pursued independence peacefully through meetings, petitions, elections and negotiation rather than violence.

mcq.questionText: Which body did Nyerere address in New York to put Tanganyika's case for independence before the world?
mcq.explanation: Nyerere petitioned and addressed the UN Trusteeship Council, using Tanganyika's trust status to press Britain to grant independence.

mcq.questionText: Which settler-supported party was formed in 1956 to oppose TANU and promote multiracialism?
mcq.explanation: The United Tanganyika Party was a multiracial, government-favoured party formed in 1956, but it failed against TANU's mass support.

mcq.questionText: In which years were the first general elections held in Tanganyika on a multiracial franchise that TANU dominated?
mcq.explanation: Elections held in 1958 and 1959 gave TANU a sweeping victory, showing its overwhelming popular support.

mcq.questionText: What position did Julius Nyerere hold when Tanganyika became independent on 9 December 1961?
mcq.explanation: At independence Nyerere served as Prime Minister; Tanganyika became a republic with him as President in 1962.

mcq.questionText: When did Tanganyika become a republic with Julius Nyerere as its first President?
mcq.explanation: On 9 December 1962, one year after independence, Tanganyika became a republic with Nyerere as the first executive President.

mcq.questionText: How did the cooperative movement help the independence struggle in Tanganyika?

options.text: It supplied weapons for an armed uprising
It united farmers economically and spread political awareness
It replaced TANU as the main political party

mcq.explanation: Cooperatives such as the KNCU and the Victoria Federation organised farmers, raised grievances against unfair prices, and helped spread nationalist ideas.

mcq.questionText: Which trade union body supported the nationalist struggle by mobilising urban workers?
mcq.explanation: The Tanganyika Federation of Labour organised workers and used strikes and protests that strengthened the pressure for independence alongside TANU.

mcq.questionText: Why was Tanganyika's path to independence relatively peaceful compared with some other African countries?

options.text: It had a very large white settler population unwilling to leave
Its trust status, strong united TANU leadership and constitutional methods eased the transfer of power
Britain had already left Africa entirely by 1950
There was no nationalist movement at all

mcq.explanation: A small settler population, UN trusteeship obligations, a united mass party using Kiswahili, and Nyerere's constitutional approach all made the transition peaceful.

fib.questionText: TANU was formed in the year _____.
fib.explanation: The Tanganyika African National Union was founded on 7 July 1954.

fib.questionText: The first president of TANU was Julius Kambarage _____.
fib.explanation: Julius Nyerere led TANU and the independence struggle.

fib.questionText: Tanganyika obtained its full independence on 9 December _____.
fib.explanation: Independence Day for Tanganyika is 9 December 1961.

fib.questionText: After the Second World War Tanganyika was administered by Britain as a United Nations _____ Territory.
fib.explanation: Tanganyika was a UN Trust (Trusteeship) Territory under British administration from 1946.

fib.questionText: TANU developed out of the earlier welfare body called the Tanganyika African _____.
fib.explanation: The Tanganyika African Association (TAA) was transformed into TANU in 1954.

fib.questionText: The language used by TANU to unite people of different tribes was _____.
fib.explanation: Kiswahili was widely spoken and helped build national unity.

fib.questionText: Tanganyika became a republic in the year _____.
fib.explanation: On 9 December 1962 Tanganyika became a republic with Nyerere as President.

fib.questionText: The settler-backed party formed in 1956 to oppose TANU was the United Tanganyika _____.
fib.explanation: The United Tanganyika Party (UTP) promoted multiracialism but lost to TANU.

fib.questionText: At independence in 1961, Julius Nyerere held the office of _____.
fib.explanation: Nyerere was Prime Minister at independence before becoming President in the 1962 republic.

fib.questionText: Workers were mobilised for the struggle through the trade union body called the Tanganyika Federation of _____.
fib.explanation: The Tanganyika Federation of Labour (TFL) organised workers in support of nationalism.

tf.questionText: Julius Nyerere led Tanganyika's independence movement through armed guerrilla war.
tf.explanation: Nyerere used peaceful, constitutional methods, not armed struggle.

tf.questionText: Tanganyika was a United Nations Trust Territory administered by France.
tf.explanation: It was administered by Britain, not France.

tf.questionText: TANU grew out of the Tanganyika African Association.
tf.explanation: TAA was transformed into TANU in 1954.

tf.questionText: TANU used Kiswahili to unite people of different ethnic groups.
tf.explanation: Kiswahili was a unifying common language used to spread the nationalist message.

tf.questionText: Tanganyika became a republic in 1961, the same day it gained independence.
tf.explanation: It became a republic in 1962, one year after independence in 1961.

tf.questionText: The United Tanganyika Party was more popular than TANU in the 1958-1959 elections.
tf.explanation: TANU won an overwhelming victory; the UTP failed badly.

tf.questionText: Cooperative unions like the Kilimanjaro Native Cooperative Union helped spread nationalist ideas among farmers.
tf.explanation: Cooperatives organised farmers economically and raised political awareness.

tf.questionText: Tanganyika's small settler population made it easier to achieve a peaceful transfer of power.
tf.explanation: Unlike settler-heavy colonies, Tanganyika faced less settler resistance, aiding a peaceful transition.

summary.questionText: State the year TANU was formed and the name of its first president.
summary.correctAnswer: TANU was formed in 1954, and its first president was Julius Nyerere.
summary.explanation: TANU (7 July 1954) was led by Julius Nyerere from its founding.

summary.questionText: What was the Tanganyika African Association (TAA) and how was it linked to TANU?
summary.correctAnswer: The TAA was an early African welfare and social association that was transformed into the political party TANU in 1954.
summary.explanation: TAA provided the membership and base that became TANU.

summary.questionText: List two main aims of TANU.
summary.correctAnswer: To achieve self-government and independence for Tanganyika, and to unite all Africans regardless of tribe.
summary.explanation: TANU sought independence and national unity through peaceful means.

summary.questionText: Describe two methods TANU used in the independence struggle.
summary.correctAnswer: It used peaceful constitutional means such as petitions and elections, and mass mobilisation using Kiswahili to unite the people.
summary.explanation: TANU avoided violence and relied on organisation, persuasion and the ballot.

summary.questionText: How did Tanganyika's status as a UN Trust Territory help the independence struggle?
summary.correctAnswer: Britain was obliged under the trusteeship to prepare Tanganyika for self-rule, and nationalists could petition the UN Trusteeship Council to press for independence.
summary.explanation: Trust status gave the nationalists an international platform and legal pressure on Britain.

summary.questionText: What role did the cooperative movement play in the struggle for independence?
summary.correctAnswer: Cooperatives organised farmers, fought unfair crop prices, and spread political awareness that supported the nationalist movement.
summary.explanation: Economic grievances raised by cooperatives strengthened the demand for self-rule.

summary.questionText: Name the dates of independence and of becoming a republic for Tanganyika.
summary.correctAnswer: Independence was on 9 December 1961, and Tanganyika became a republic on 9 December 1962.
summary.explanation: These two milestones came exactly one year apart.

summary.questionText: What was the result of the 1958-1959 elections for TANU?
summary.correctAnswer: TANU won an overwhelming victory, proving its mass popular support and speeding the move toward self-government.
summary.explanation: The landslide showed that TANU represented the people and weakened opposition parties.

summary.questionText: Explain why Kiswahili was important in TANU's work.
summary.correctAnswer: Kiswahili was understood by many tribes, so it allowed TANU to communicate widely and build national unity beyond ethnic divisions.
summary.explanation: A common language overcame tribal barriers and unified the movement.

summary.questionText: Give two factors that made Tanganyika's independence relatively peaceful.
summary.correctAnswer: A small white settler population and a strong, united TANU under Nyerere using peaceful constitutional methods, helped by UN trusteeship pressure.
summary.explanation: Less settler resistance and disciplined nationalist leadership eased the transfer of power.

hoq.questionText: Why was the use of Kiswahili a more effective tool for TANU than relying on English in mobilising the masses for independence?

options.text: English was banned by the British in Tanganyika
Kiswahili crossed tribal boundaries and was understood by ordinary people, enabling wide mass mobilisation and unity
Kiswahili was the only language spoken by colonial officials
English was unknown anywhere in East Africa

hoq.explanation: Kiswahili was a widely shared language among many ethnic groups, so it let TANU reach and unite ordinary people, while English was limited to the educated few.

hoq.questionText: Which combination of factors best explains why Tanganyika achieved independence more peacefully than settler colonies such as Kenya?

options.text: A large armed rebellion and many settlers
A small settler population, UN trusteeship obligations on Britain, and a united party using constitutional methods
Total absence of any political organisation
Strong support from European settlers for African rule

hoq.explanation: Few settlers meant less resistance, trusteeship created international pressure, and a united TANU using peaceful means allowed a negotiated transfer of power.

hoq.questionText: How did the UN Trusteeship system give Tanganyikan nationalists an advantage that nationalists in ordinary colonies did not have?

options.text: It allowed them to legally petition and address an international body that obliged Britain to prepare them for self-rule
It gave them weapons to fight the British army
It made Tanganyika a permanent German colony
It removed all Africans from political life

hoq.explanation: As a trust territory, Tanganyika's nationalists could appeal directly to the UN Trusteeship Council, creating legal and international pressure on Britain to advance independence.
